title: The economics of investment expensing
content:
In July 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act made 100% equipment expensing permanent after two decades of temporary bonus depreciation. I evaluate this reform in a general-equilibrium heterogeneous-firm model with collateral constraints and nonrefundable tax deductions. When matched to U.S. tax-return and Compustat moments, the model yields three findings. First, permanent expensing raises long-run capital by 4.5% and output and real wages by 1.1%, roughly double the gains without financial frictions. Per present-value dollar of forgone corporate tax revenue, expensing builds 5.6 times as much capital as a tax rate cut, versus 3.4 times without financial frictions. Second, first-year capital purchases are U-shaped in firm age: young constrained firms and mature profitable firms expand, whereas unconstrained middle-aged firms whose investment exceeds taxable income delay purchases. Third, making expensing permanent gives up countercyclical bonus depreciation; enacted at the onset of a recession, a two-year bonus offsets 44% of the five-year investment drop.

Here is the paper by Doruk Gökalp, who is on the job market this year from NYU.
